newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil steps up the pace of telcommunications selloffs.
newsitem.headline: Brazil steps up the pace of telcommunications selloffs.

text.p: Brazil will speed up the privatisation of its massive telecommunications industry, and the process may be completed by the middle of next year, Communications Minister Sergio Motta said Tuesday.
"We're entering the final phase of the privatisation process," Motta told reporters after officials agreed on a new blueprint for the sale of the $100 billion-rated Telebras system.

"We expect that by the end of the first quarter, or at least within the first four months (of 1998), we will hold the first auction," the minister said. "Our expectation is that in the first half we will finish off the auctions."
Previously, the government had hoped to sell one or two Telebras subsidiaries before concentrating on the October 1998 elections for president, congress and state govenors.
"This represents a big acceleration of the process," a Communications Ministry spokesman said after Motta's speech. "It's an entirely acheivable projection."

The announcement comes on the heels of the governments' success in rushing new telecommunications legislation through Congress and the spectacular auction earlier this month of a Sao Paulo city cellular telephone concession for $2.45 billion to a group including Atlanta-based BellSouth Corp.

Stock market investors have been clamouring for a piece of Brazil's telecommunications pie too, with demand for Telebras stock one of the main factors behind a roughly 60 percent surge on the Sao Paulo stock exchange so far this year.

Motta, who has been at the centre of a political storm this week over blunt criticisms over the government's allies in Congress, kept an uncharacteristic silence after the news conference and did not answer reporters' questions.
Instead, he handed out a timetable of steps to be taken ahead of the long-awaited privatisation of Telebras.

The schedule was due to begin Aug. 10 with the selection of directors for the National Telecommunications Agency, a new regulatory agency which will take on many of the Communications Ministry's duties for overseeing the industry.
The agency was slated to begin working Sept. 1.

Another key step would take place Oct. 30 when the government was due to invite consulting companies to bid for contracts to advise on the privatisation of one or more of the Telebras units to be sold.
The first consulting contract or contracts would be signed by the end of the year, paving the way for the privatisations themselves, Motta said.

The minister also suprised reporters who cover telecommunications by saying the government might split Telebras into less than the four regional units it had been expected to create prior to privatisation.
"Today we're reopening this discussion, with a view of reducing the number of units," Motta said. He added, however, that the number would not be so low as to restrict competition in the sector.
